title: UK Global Talent Visa Requirements 2026: Endorsement Guide
metaDescription: UK Global Talent visa 2026: 70 points, endorsement from one of six bodies, £524 plus £766 fees, no job offer or English test, ILR in 3 or 5 years.
headline: UK Global Talent Visa Requirements 2026: Full Guide

sections.title: What is the Global Talent visa?
sections.content:
The UK Global Talent visa is the most flexible UK immigration route for leaders and future leaders in science, engineering, medicine, humanities, digital technology and arts and culture. There is no sponsor, no job offer, no salary threshold and no English language test at the initial stage. Instead, you must score 70 points: 10 for working in an eligible field and 60 for a successful endorsement, or for winning a recognised prestigious prize.

The route runs in two stages. First you apply for endorsement, and the Home Office refers your case to the relevant endorsing body. Once endorsed, you apply for the visa itself, which must be made within three months of the endorsement letter. Winners of a prize named on the Home Office list can skip endorsement and apply directly.

sections.title: The six endorsing bodies
sections.content:
There are six endorsing bodies, each with its own published criteria. Tech Nation assesses digital technology, the Royal Society covers natural sciences and medical research, the British Academy covers humanities and social sciences, and the Royal Academy of Engineering covers engineering. UK Research and Innovation offers a standard route and an endorsed-funder route, and Arts Council England covers arts and culture, including architecture, fashion, film and design.

A design category was added in March 2026, and the prestigious prizes list was expanded the same year. AI and cybersecurity applications are now fast-tracked, with endorsement decisions in about three weeks, while other digital technology cases typically take five to eight weeks and arts cases up to eight weeks.

sections.title: Evidence: Talent versus Promise
sections.content:
Endorsement is assessed at two levels. Exceptional Talent is for established leaders, and Exceptional Promise is for early-career applicants showing the potential to become leaders. For digital technology, Tech Nation asks for a mandatory criterion, recognition as a leading talent or potential leading talent, plus optional criteria covering product impact, technical contribution, commercial impact and contribution outside your immediate work.

Evidence must be specific, attributable and recent, typically within the last five years. A strong application usually includes three substantive recommendation letters and a portfolio of about ten pieces of evidence. The endorsement carries the entire weight of the application, so weak or vague evidence is the most common reason for refusal.

sections.title: Costs, length and settlement
sections.content:
The endorsement fee is £524, payable to the Home Office when you apply, and the visa fee is £766, with the immigration health surcharge paid on top for each year of the visa. Permission runs for up to five years at a time, with no cap on total stay, and you can work for any employer, be self-employed or run a business.

Settlement, or Indefinite Leave to Remain, comes after three years for Exceptional Talent in digital technology, arts and culture and architecture, and for both Talent and Promise applicants endorsed by the Royal Society, British Academy, Royal Academy of Engineering or UKRI in research routes. Exceptional Promise in digital technology, arts and culture and architecture follows a five-year clock.

faqs.q: Do I need a job offer for the Global Talent visa?
faqs.a: No, the Global Talent visa needs no job offer, no sponsor and no minimum salary at any stage, and there is no English language test when you first apply. What it demands is evidence of achievement, assessed by an expert endorsing body, plus the ordinary suitability checks that apply to every visa route. You must be at least 18 and work in an eligible field.

faqs.q: How much does the Global Talent visa cost in 2026?
faqs.a: The endorsement fee is £524 and the visa fee is £766, a total of £1,290 in Home Office fees, plus the immigration health surcharge for each year of the visa. Fees rose on 8 April 2026 and are paid per person when you apply. Some guides quote £766 as the total because the endorsement fee is sometimes described separately, so budget for both stages.

faqs.q: How long does Global Talent endorsement take?
faqs.a: Endorsement decisions typically take five to eight weeks for digital technology, up to eight weeks for arts and culture, and two to five weeks for academia and research, with a two-week fast track for eligible researchers. AI and cybersecurity applications are fast-tracked to about three weeks. The visa application itself follows once endorsement is granted, and must be made within three months.

faqs.q: Can I settle in the UK on a Global Talent visa?
faqs.a: Yes, settlement comes after three or five years depending on who endorsed you and under which criteria. Exceptional Talent in digital technology, arts and culture and architecture qualifies after three years, as do both Talent and Promise applicants endorsed by the research bodies. Exceptional Promise in digital technology, arts and culture and architecture follows a five-year clock.
